name: Wipro
h1: Turning AI-native ambition into connected delivery
lede: Wipro has stood up an AI-Native Business and Platforms Unit and is working to convert a large-deal pipeline. Airtable gives delivery, sales and platform teams one shared way to run that work.
why_h2: An AI-first pivot with deals to land
why_p: 2026 has brought a new AI-native unit, steady results and a sharp swing in large-deal bookings.

signals.title: Large-deal bookings drop in Q2 FY27
signals.body: Large-deal bookings fell 58.6 per cent sequentially to US$674 million, with two major contracts not signed before quarter end and expected in Q3.
signals.angle: When conversion timing matters, one view of every pursuit, owner and approval step helps deals close on schedule.

signals.title: Q1 FY27: 13 large deals worth US$1.6 billion
signals.body: Wipro reported large-deal bookings of US$1.6 billion in Q1 FY27, up 12.9 per cent quarter on quarter, across 13 large deals.
signals.angle: Each large deal becomes a transition programme. Airtable keeps onboarding, staffing and client milestones in one connected tracker.

signals.title: AI-Native Business and Platforms Unit
signals.body: Wipro formed a unit to own and scale assets from the Wipro Intelligence suite, including the WINGS and WEGA delivery platforms, and to incubate AI-led businesses.
signals.angle: Platform portfolios need a shared record of assets, roadmaps and client deployments that sales and delivery can both use.

signals.title: FY26 results and a ₹150 billion buyback
signals.body: Wipro reported FY26 net profit of ₹13,265.5 crore, up 0.4 per cent, and announced a ₹150 billion share buyback.
signals.angle: Flat-growth years reward operational efficiency. Consolidating internal trackers onto one layer removes manual reporting effort.
